claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain in polycrystalline tungsten is governed by the formation and mobility of helium-vacancy clusters.
High-temperature toughness in polycrystalline tungsten is governed by the formation and mobility of helium-vacancy clusters.
High-temperature helium-ion irradiation of polycrystalline tungsten produces helium-vacancy clusters.
Helium-vacancy cluster mobility reduces the energy required for dislocation glide.
Reducing the energy required for dislocation glide enhances high-temperature plastic strain.
Reducing the energy required for dislocation glide enhances toughness.
Helium-ion-irradiated polycrystalline tungsten will exhibit greater high-temperature plastic strain than unirradiated polycrystalline tungsten.
Helium-ion-irradiated polycrystalline tungsten will exhibit greater toughness than unirradiated polycrystalline tungsten.
The hypothesis is proposed to hold from 500 to 1000 degrees Celsius.
The hypothesis is proposed to hold for helium-ion fluences from 10^20 to 10^22 ions per square metre.
The controlled comparison uses unirradiated polycrystalline tungsten as the baseline for irradiated polycrystalline tungsten.
No significant difference in both high-temperature plastic strain and toughness between irradiated and unirradiated samples would falsify the predicted enhancement.
